name: MAX7221CWG+T
title: MAX7219/MAX7221: 8-digit common-cathode LED display drivers with serial interface
summary: Serial-input drivers for common-cathode LED displays: up to eight 7-segment digits with decimal points, a bar graph, or 64 single LEDs. Each chip holds a code-B decoder, multiplexed scan logic, eight 8-bit digit registers in SRAM and the segment and digit drivers; one resistor sets the peak current of all segments, and a 16-step PWM register trims brightness. A 150 µA shutdown keeps register data, the display starts blank at power-up, and a 10 MHz three-wire port can be chained through DOUT. The MAX7221 adds slew-limited segment drivers and a chip-select port that is fully SPI compatible; MAX7219EWG is the MAX7219 in 24-pin wide SO for -40°C to +85°C.
key_figures: -40 mA typ (-30 to -45 mA) with RSET = 9.53 kΩ
RSET plus 16-step PWM (31/32 to 1/32 MAX7219, 15/16 to 1/16 MAX7221)
24-pin narrow plastic DIP, wide SO, narrow CERDIP; dice

notes: Dice (C/D) are specified only at TA = +25°C.

MAX7219 and MAX7221 differ in two ways only: the MAX7221 limits the slew rate of its segment drivers to cut EMI, and its CS input makes the serial port fully SPI compatible (SPI, QSPI, MICROWIRE). Off-state drivers of the MAX7219 are pulled to a rail; those of the MAX7221 float.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: One MAX7219 or MAX7221 runs an eight-digit common-cathode 7-segment display from a microprocessor over three wires: data into DIN, a port line on LOAD (CS), and the clock on CLK. A single 9.53 kΩ resistor from +5 V to ISET sets the peak segment current; the eight digit lines go to the digit cathodes and the eight segment lines (A–G and DP) to the segment anodes.
notes: The same circuit serves the MAX7221, with CS in place of LOAD.

circuits.title: Driving 2.3 in displays with external digit transistors
circuits.description: Two large AND2307SLC digits are driven with the chip's own segment outputs but with IRF540 MOSFETs in place of its digit drivers. DIG 0 and DIG 1 serve only as logic signals into a MAX394 analog switch, which swings each MOSFET gate between +5 V (through its NC input) and -5 V (through NO); each MOSFET pulls one display's cathode to -5 V and a 4.7 kΩ resistor pulls it up to +5 V when off. Because the segments of these displays drop about 8 V and the decimal point about 4.2 V, a 5.6 V zener sits in series with the decimal-point line. With external transistors sinking the digit current, 45 mA peak segment current is allowed even with only two digits scanned. RSET is 30 kΩ, with 0.1 µF bypass on V+.

circuits.title: Two cascaded drivers for 16 seven-segment digits
circuits.description: Two drivers share one three-wire port to run sixteen digits on two eight-digit displays. DOUT of the first feeds DIN of the second; LOAD (CS) and CLK of both are tied to common LOAD DATA and CLOCK lines. Each chip has its own 9.53 kΩ RSET from +5 V to ISET and a 0.1 µF capacitor from V+ to ground. Through the no-op register one chip can be written while the other is left unchanged.

operation.text: The two devices match in every respect but two. The MAX7221's segment outputs have a controlled current slew rate for lower EMI, and its CS input gates the clock, giving a port fully compatible with SPI. When off, MAX7219 digit outputs go to V+ and segment outputs to GND; on the MAX7221 both go high-impedance. For 3 V supplies or blinking segments the MAX6951 is offered instead.

Data arrives as 16-bit words, most significant bit (D15) first. D15–D12 are ignored, D11–D8 hold the register address and D7–D0 the data. On the MAX7219 every rising CLK edge shifts DIN in, whatever LOAD is doing; on the MAX7221 CS must be low for data to move in or out. The word in the shift register is copied to the addressed register when LOAD/CS goes high, which has to arrive on or after the 16th rising clock edge and before the 17th, otherwise the data is lost. Bits leave on DOUT on falling CLK edges, 16.5 clocks after they entered DIN.

Fourteen registers are addressable: eight digit registers, held in an on-chip 8x8 dual-port SRAM, plus no-op, decode mode, intensity, scan limit, shutdown and display test. Each digit can be rewritten on its own. The SRAM keeps its contents as long as V+ stays above about 2 V (typical).

In shutdown the scan oscillator stops and the display goes dark: on the MAX7219 the segment outputs are pulled to ground and the digit outputs to V+, on the MAX7221 both float. Digit and control register contents are kept, and registers can still be written. Leaving shutdown typically takes under 250 µs. Display test overrides shutdown. Entering and leaving shutdown repeatedly flashes the display. Supply current in shutdown is lowest with the logic inputs held at GND or V+.

At power-up every control register is reset, the display is blank and the part sits in shutdown. Unless it is programmed first, it then scans a single digit, does not decode, and has intensity at its minimum.

One bit per digit chooses code B decoding (1) or raw segment data (0). With code B, only D3–D0 of the digit register are read and D4–D6 are ignored, giving the characters 0–9, E, H, L, P, minus and blank; D7 drives the decimal point directly, 1 for on. Without decoding, each data bit drives one segment line: D7 is DP, D6 is A, and so on down to D0 for G.

Brightness is set two ways. Analog: RSET between V+ and ISET fixes the peak segment current at nominally 100 times the ISET current; it may be a fixed or a variable resistor, and must be at least 9.53 kΩ, which typically gives 40 mA. Digital: the low four bits of the intensity register drive an internal pulse-width modulator that divides the average segment current in 16 steps, ranging from 31/32 down to 1/32 of the peak on the MAX7219 and from 15/16 down to 1/16 on the MAX7221. Between digits the display is blanked for at least 1/32 of a cycle.

The scan-limit register selects how many digits (1 to 8) are multiplexed. With all eight the scan rate is typically 800 Hz; with fewer it rises to 8 fOSC/N. Brightness depends on the number of digits scanned, so the scan limit is not meant for blanking digits such as leading zeros. With three or fewer digits each digit driver dissipates too much unless the segment current is reduced through RSET: 10, 20 and 30 mA maximum for 1, 2 and 3 digits when the internal digit drivers carry the current.

Display-test mode lights every LED by overriding all control and digit registers, shutdown included, without changing them. It scans all 8 digits at 31/32 duty (15/16 on the MAX7221) and remains until the display-test register is written back to normal.

Several drivers chain by joining every LOAD/CS line and wiring each DOUT, a CMOS logic output, to the next DIN. To write one chip in a chain of four, send its 16-bit word followed by three no-op words; when LOAD/CS rises every chip latches, the three others receive a no-op and the target its data. If the digit count is not a multiple of 8, give both drivers the same scan limit so the displays match in brightness: for 12 digits, 6 per display (1/6 duty per digit each); for 11 digits, both set to 6 with one digit driver left unconnected. Splitting 6 and 5 would make the 5-digit display brighter (1/5 against 1/6).

Peak digit currents cause supply ripple; a 10 µF electrolytic and a 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor are placed from V+ to GND, right at the chip. The driver sits close to the display with short connections to limit wiring inductance and EMI. Both GND pins are connected to ground.

Segment current is roughly 100 times the ISET current; the RSET table gives values for 10 to 40 mA and LED forward voltages from 1.5 V to 3.5 V. The highest recommended segment current is 40 mA. Above that, external digit drivers take the current and the chip acts as the controller. When external current sources drive the segments, RSET = 47 kΩ saves power. When the internal digit drivers sink the current and fewer than four digits are scanned, the 1-, 2- and 3-digit current limits apply. The power-dissipation ratings set the allowed combination of ambient temperature, segment current and LED forward voltage.
Die size 0.093 in (2.36 mm) by 0.080 in (2.03 mm); 5267 transistors; substrate connected to GND.
